# axiolid-hidden-lines

Exact scalar hidden-line drawings of triangle meshes in orthographic and perspective views, and visible face regions in orthographic views.

## Overview

The exact scalar provider for `MeshHiddenLines` (ADR 0090): the visible and
hidden pieces of the boundary, silhouette and crease edges of triangle
meshes (and, when selected, the edges between face groups, ADR 0106) in an orthographic or perspective view. Visibility is decided exactly in the view's
affine frame, with the interval filter first and dyadic big integers when it
cannot decide; no tolerance enters a decision, and the output endpoints are
the exact points rounded once. It refuses what it cannot decide with a typed
error that names the mesh. Candidate pairs are found in an `axiolid-spatial` BVH over view-space boxes
(worst case still edges times triangles); the examined pairs are bounded by
`max_candidate_pairs`. A
near clipping plane that cuts a `Solid` mesh leaves a cap that occludes, decided
by exact ray parity with a symbolic perturbation of the image point; a face of a
cut solid in the plane needs no special case. A solid wholly beyond the plane is
removed.
It also draws perspective views (ADR 0107): a pinhole at the frame origin
with `near` below zero, decided with exact determinants of vectors from the
eye, the cap by parity along the eye ray. It does not draw exact B-rep edges
or smooth silhouettes. The visible-face provider refuses perspective views by
name.

`ScalarVisibleFaces` is the provider for `MeshVisibleFaces` (ADR 0094): the
visible face regions of caller-grouped triangles in the same view, with the
same preparation, clipping, caps and crop. The visible outlines, the clip
lines, the crop and the exact intersection curves of the triangles go into
the exact planar arrangement of `axiolid-exact-arrangement`; each side of
each piece is labelled by the exact frontmost source at a symbolic side
point, and the regions are traced from those labels. Region vertices are the
exact points rounded once where no edge passes through the rounding cell of
another vertex, and snap-rounded to the binary64 grid otherwise (ADR 0100).
Sources tied in depth each receive the area. The groups are the caller's per
triangle or, as `FaceGroups::Planar`, derived exactly: triangles join across
an edge of exactly two triangles with parallel, same-facing normals, and a
group is named by its smallest triangle (ADR 0106).
A region whose area collapses under rounding is dropped and counted in the
evidence, never refused.

Both providers honour see-through triangles (ADR 0111). A see-through
triangle hides nothing. A visible hidden-line piece counts the see-through
triangles strictly in front of it, decided with the perturbed image point of
the caps, so panes sharing a diagonal count once. A visible-face region of a
see-through source lists its stack: the surfaces behind it in exact depth
layers down to the first opaque triangle or cap, found with a counted linear
pass and a binary insertion; a face group must be all opaque or all
see-through, and planar groups never join triangles of different occlusion.
The cap of a cut solid occludes whatever its triangles' flags. Without a
see-through triangle the drawing, the regions, the evidence and the exact
work are unchanged.

## Changes

Latest release, 0.1.6 (2026-11-14):

### Added

- `ScalarHiddenLines` and `ScanHiddenLines` honour see-through triangles and
  claim them through `supports_occlusion` (ADR 0111, #496). A see-through
  triangle hides nothing; a visible piece counts in `seen_through` the
  see-through triangles of nonzero image area whose plane is strictly in
  front of it and whose image holds the point shifted by `(ε, ε²)`, decided
  with the perturbed image-side clips of the caps, in orthographic and
  perspective views. A visible gap is split where that count changes, found
  by one sweep over the sorted span ends (O(G log G) exact comparisons for G
  see-through spans over an edge), and a hidden piece is not split. Without a see-through triangle no step of this
  runs: the drawing, the evidence and the exact work are unchanged. A
  `PerTriangle` occlusion slice of the wrong length, or an unknown occlusion
  mode, is `InvalidInput` naming the mesh.
- `ScalarVisibleFaces`, `ScanVisibleFaces` and `UnprunedVisibleFaces` honour
  see-through triangles and claim them (ADR 0111, #496). A side whose front
  holds a see-through triangle gets its stack: the other candidates grouped
  into exact depth layers down to the first one holding an opaque triangle or
  a cap, found by one linear pass for the occluder and a binary insertion for
  the layers between; each of these extra depth comparisons counts against
  `max_candidate_pairs`. A region is a maximal region of one source and one
  stack, `VisibleRegion::behind` lists the stack without the region's own
  layer-0 entry, the output breaks a tie of mesh, source and outer ring by
  `behind`, and `tied_sides` also counts a side with a tie behind its front.
  The entries are bounded by `max_behind_surfaces` (`BudgetExceeded`,
  `visible-face behind surfaces`). The prune keeps every edge behind a
  see-through triangle, since it hides nothing. A face group that mixes
  see-through and opaque triangles is `InvalidInput` naming the mesh, and
  `FaceGroups::Planar` joins two triangles only when their occlusion is
  equal. Without a see-through triangle no extra comparison is made and the
  regions and evidence are unchanged.
- `scenario/hidden-lines` and `scenario/visible-faces` gain a
  `glazed-isometric` grid, the isometric one with every third box wholly
  see-through, and print a drawing hash that leaves out an empty count or
  stack, so the opaque scenes print what they printed before (#496); they
  did, hash, escalations and pairs alike. Three runs each on a loaded machine
  (median of each run, BVH provider, against the opaque isometric grid of the
  same size): hidden lines 400 boxes 0.50-0.52 s against 0.27-0.39 s (79,064
  to 94,509 pairs), 2,500 boxes 2.33-3.29 s against 2.50-2.51 s (511,016 to
  617,263 pairs); visible faces 100 boxes 0.34-0.36 s against 0.23-0.30 s
  (1,266 to 2,001 pieces, 142 surfaces behind), 400 boxes 1.18-1.92 s against
  1.25-1.30 s (4,938 to 11,097 pieces, 383,574 to 789,043 pairs, 1,931
  surfaces behind). Edges behind glass lose the early-out of full cover and
  are no longer pruned from the arrangement, which the counts show; the run
  to run spread on this machine is as large as the cost. These timings were
  taken before the count became a sweep over the sorted span ends; the
  drawings are the same since.
